items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I talk with Wynton Marsalis a lot about this because he doesn’t know — he knows Earle Warren but didn’t realize that if he led the reeds in that band he must be great.

ctx.x: It does. It also means Eddie Durham is as great as I say he is, and he is. So it was Eddie Durham in the trombones and Benny Morton and Dicky Wills. I wasn’t too close with Vic. Vic was kind of shy I betcha. And to get children into his inner circle, he liked to talk to musicians and adults. And so, and I had such a friendship with Dicky Wells that took me all around. Dicky is my meal ticket, my ace — and he was so brilliant. Dicky Wells was wise too but Eddie Durham was the genius and wrote all that stuff. And…

of his musical greatness — was that you know adolescents are rebellious. They’re not necessarily political or socially oriented. I mean I think the youth movement concept is a little bit overrated. It happened in my generation in America and perhaps even internationally but it doesn’t always happen.
